saints.name: St. Bede the Venerable
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The monk of Jarrow whose history first told the story of the English Church, the “Father of English History”…
biography: Given as a boy to the monastery of Wearmouth-Jarrow in Northumbria, Bede spent his whole life there in study, teaching, and prayer. From that small cloister he produced commentaries on Scripture, works on chronology and computation, and above all the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, the chief source for the early Christian history of England.

He completed his last work, a translation of the Gospel of John, on the very day he died in 735, dictating its final words to a scribe. Honored as “Venerable” from soon after his death, he was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1899, the only Englishman so named.
saints.knownFor: His Ecclesiastical History of the English People.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1899)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 May
